title: Parahoric Reductive Quotient for Sp(W)
body_html:
Parahoric Reductive Quotient for Sp(W)

Let \(W\) be a symplectic \(F\)-space with residue field \(k\), and \(G=\operatorname{Sp}(W)\). A point \(x\in\mathcal B(\operatorname{Sp}(W))\) is a self-dual lattice function \(\mathscr L_x\); write \(\mathscr L_{x,r}:=\mathscr L_x(r)\) for its value at level \(r\). It has period \(\mathscr L_{x,s+1}=\mathfrak p\,\mathscr L_{x,s}\) and self-duality \[ \mathscr L_{x,s}^{\#}=\mathscr L_{x,(-s)+},\qquad L^{\#}=\{w\in W:\langle w,L\rangle\subseteq\mathfrak p\} \] (conductor-\(\mathfrak p\) convention; see Self-Dual Lattice Function).

Graded pieces

For \(s\in\mathbb R\) set \[ \operatorname{gr}_s\mathscr L_x:=\mathscr L_{x,s}/\mathscr L_{x,s+}, \] a finite-dimensional \(k\)-vector space, nonzero exactly at the jumps of \(\mathscr L_x\). Multiplication by \(\varpi\) gives \(\operatorname{gr}_{s+1}\mathscr L_x\cong\operatorname{gr}_s\mathscr L_x\), so it suffices to look at \(s\in[0,1)\).

The symplectic form reduces modulo \(\mathfrak p\) to a perfect \(k\)-pairing \[ \operatorname{gr}_{-s}\mathscr L_x\times\operatorname{gr}_{s}\mathscr L_x\longrightarrow k, \qquad (\bar u,\bar v)\mapsto\langle u,v\rangle\bmod\mathfrak p . \] Hence the jump set is symmetric under \(s\mapsto -s\), and within \([0,1)\) the jumps split into three kinds:

  • \(s\equiv 0\): the pairing is \(\operatorname{gr}_0\mathscr L_x\times\operatorname{gr}_0\mathscr L_x\to k\), alternating, so \(\operatorname{gr}_0\mathscr L_x\) is a finite symplectic \(k\)-space.
  • \(s\equiv\tfrac12\): here \(-s\equiv s\), so \(\operatorname{gr}_{1/2}\mathscr L_x\) self-pairs through \(\varpi\); since \(\varpi\langle\,,\,\rangle\) is still alternating, \(\operatorname{gr}_{1/2}\mathscr L_x\) is a finite symplectic \(k\)-space.
  • \(0<s<\tfrac12\): \(\operatorname{gr}_{s}\mathscr L_x\) pairs perfectly with the distinct piece \(\operatorname{gr}_{-s}\mathscr L_x\), giving \(\operatorname{gr}_{-s}\mathscr L_x\cong(\operatorname{gr}_s\mathscr L_x)^{*}\).

Parahoric and reductive quotient

The Moy–Prasad groups attached to \(x\) are \[ G_{x,0}=\{g\in\operatorname{Sp}(W):g\mathscr L_{x,s}=\mathscr L_{x,s}\ \forall s\},\qquad G_{x,0+}=\{g\in G_{x,0}:(g-1)\mathscr L_{x,s}\subseteq\mathscr L_{x,s+}\ \forall s\}. \] Since \(\operatorname{Sp}(W)\) is simply connected, \(G_{x,0}\) is the full stabilizer of \(x\) and the quotient is connected. The action on the graded pieces, preserving the forms and dualities above, induces a canonical isomorphism of finite reductive groups over \(k\): \[ \boxed{\;\mathsf G_x:=G_{x,0}/G_{x,0+}\;\cong\; \operatorname{Sp}\!\big(\operatorname{gr}_0\mathscr L_x\big)\times \operatorname{Sp}\!\big(\operatorname{gr}_{1/2}\mathscr L_x\big)\times \prod_{0<s<1/2}\operatorname{GL}\!\big(\operatorname{gr}_s\mathscr L_x\big).\;} \] The two \(\operatorname{Sp}\) factors are the two self-dual levels \(s\equiv 0\) and \(s\equiv\tfrac12\) (the two ends of the local Dynkin diagram of type \(\widetilde C_n\)); either factor is trivial when that level is not a jump. Each interior jump pair \(\{s,-s\}\) contributes one \(\operatorname{GL}(\operatorname{gr}_s\mathscr L_x)\), acting on \(\operatorname{gr}_{-s}\mathscr L_x\) by the contragredient.

With \(\dim\operatorname{gr}_0\mathscr L_x=2a\) and \(\dim\operatorname{gr}_{1/2}\mathscr L_x=2b\), \[ 2a+2b+2\!\!\sum_{0<s<1/2}\dim\operatorname{gr}_s\mathscr L_x=\dim_F W . \]

Relation to the generalized lattice model

The lattice-model finite symplectic space is the level-\(0\) factor: \[ \mathsf b_x=\mathscr L_{x,0}/\mathscr L_{x,0}^{\#}=\mathscr L_{x,0}/\mathscr L_{x,0+}=\operatorname{gr}_0\mathscr L_x , \] so the finite Weil representation \(S(\mathsf b_x)\) used in Generalized Lattice Model is the Weil representation of the first factor \(\operatorname{Sp}(\operatorname{gr}_0\mathscr L_x)\). The remaining factors \(\operatorname{Sp}(\operatorname{gr}_{1/2}\mathscr L_x)\) and \(\operatorname{GL}(\operatorname{gr}_s\mathscr L_x)\) act on the \(W\)-support of the model functions rather than on the \(S(\mathsf b_x)\)-values.
proof_html: This is the symplectic specialization of Reductive Quotient of a Self-Dual Lattice Function. By definition \(G_{x,0+}\) acts trivially on each \(\operatorname{gr}_s\mathscr L_x\), so \(\mathsf G_x\) embeds into \(\prod_s\operatorname{GL}(\operatorname{gr}_s\mathscr L_x)\). Self-duality identifies \(\operatorname{gr}_{-s}\mathscr L_x\) with \((\operatorname{gr}_s\mathscr L_x)^{*}\) and equips the levels \(s\equiv 0,\tfrac12\) with nondegenerate alternating forms; the image is exactly the subgroup preserving these data, which is the displayed product. Surjectivity is the standard Bruhat–Tits description of the parahoric reductive quotient. \(\square\)
